question: On 24 December 2023, almost 200 people were killed and hundreds wounded in violent attacks on predominantly Christian villages in Plateau State, Nigeria. 1.

Does the Vice-President of the Commission / High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy (VP/HR) agree that these were targeted attacks against Christians, considering that they were well-coordinated attacks around Christmas and that they are believed to have been perpetrated by local Fulani herdsmen and Boko Haram in collaboration?
How does the VP/HR assess the commitment of the Nigerian authorities to combating the aforementioned violence and to protecting Christians in this country?
How can the EU and the EU Special Envoy for the promotion of freedom of religion or belief outside the EU increase their efforts to combat persistent violence against Christians in Nigeria?
answer: Clashes between farmers and herders in central Nigeria are turning increasingly violent. Central Plateau, the region around Mangu, had so far been spared, but since December 2023, events of devastating violence, with frequent attacks on places of worship, in particular against Christian communities. The authorities have reacted swiftly to the attacks in December 2023.

The Vice-President of Nigeria visited the region and expressed regret and condolences. Governor Caleb Mutfwang has declared curfews from time to time. The criminal justice response has seen a number of alleged perpetrators arrested. More broadly, President Tinubu has made improving security across Nigeria a priority.

The EU prioritises governance, security and peace in its cooperation with Nigeria and closely follows related reform efforts of the incoming government. Several EU-funded actions, also in Plateau state, aim to expand local peace infrastructures and work on community-level conflict and resource management, while strengthening the judiciary and civil society.

Freedom of religion and belief (FoRB) is a priority in the EU’s Human Rights Strategy for Nigeri a (1), and partners receive EU support to work on this issue. The EU FoRB Special Envoy is currently considering a visit to Nigeria in the coming months.
